title: Trump Pardons Steven Benjamin Floyd on January 19, 2021
description_short: Trump granted a presidential pardon to Steven Benjamin Floyd as part of a clemency list.
description_medium: The Justice Department’s clemency list records that Donald Trump pardoned Steven Benjamin Floyd on January 19, 2021. It identifies Floyd’s 2008 Southern District of Mississippi conviction for bank robbery by extortion and lists a sentence of 30 months, with the final six months in a halfway house, three years of supervised release and a $2,500 fine. The index establishes the conviction label, sentence and pardon date, but gives no account of the underlying offense or the reason for clemency. No motive should be inferred from the grant alone.
description_long: On January 19, 2021, Donald Trump pardoned Steven Benjamin Floyd, listed by the Justice Department’s Office of the Pardon Attorney under that date. The DOJ list identifies a Southern District of Mississippi bank-robbery-by-extortion case and records a sentence imposed January 3, 2008: 30 months, with the last six months in a halfway house, three years’ supervised release and a $2,500 fine. A contemporaneous Mississippi report says Floyd joined the Marine Corps at 17, served in combat in Iraq and pleaded guilty to one count of bank robbery by extortion. In reproducing Trump’s pardon announcement, the report says Floyd had been released from prison in 2009, was raising a family and owned a car-repair business; it also says the announcement credited him with helping extinguish fires during recent unrest and repairing cars without charge for widows and disabled veterans. The announcement thanked him for his military service and community commitment. Those details provide the public context cited in the announcement alongside the pardon, but the sources do not explain how they figured in the clemency decision. The DOJ list and report do not describe the robbery or identify a victim.
